items.title: 9.8.2 Salts of strong acids and weak bases

blocks.text: For salts derived from strong acids and weak bases (e.g., ammonium chloride, NH₄Cl), The conjugate base of the strong acid (e.g., Cl⁻) does not react with water. The conjugate acid of the weak base (e.g., NH₄⁺ from NH₃) reacts with water to produce H₃O⁺ ions, making the solution acidic.
NH₄⁺ is the conjugate acid of NH₃ (a weak base) and reacts with water:
Cl⁻ is the conjugate base of HCl (a strong acid) and does not affect the pH.
The solution is acidic due to the NH₄⁺ ion.
